name: Wearable artificial kidney
subtitle: a belt-worn kidney that reuses its fluid

effects.effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas

effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
how: Dialysis patients spend three sessions a week tied to a machine that uses hundreds of litres of water, because there is no small way to clean the used fluid. In a belt-worn unit, waste seeps out of the blood through a membrane, an enzyme breaks the urea into ammonia, and crystal sponges that grab ammonia lock it away, so one litre of fluid can be cleaned and reused all day.
obstacle: Holding a day's ammonia needs more sponge than a person can comfortably wear, and any leak back into the blood is dangerous.
why: Wearable kidneys stalled on removing urea; ammonia-grabbing crystals never tried for it.
real: MOFs (UiO-66, MOF-808/GO) are studied as urea and uremic-toxin sorbents for wearable-kidney dialysate regeneration, but no wearable unit with MOF ammonia adsorption was found.
